protocol: decision 2026-07-14: outputs frozen BEFORE field visit; this file is never edited
context:
CONTEXT for this pre-registration. This is metadata around the frozen
cloud-unit numbers. It does not alter any frozen number, and it contains
no real-world units or scale; the tape value and the derived multiplier
go in the later comparison file.

1. NOT scale-blind. The ridge span used as the scale candidate (length:r6,7)
   was tape-measured on site BEFORE this freeze, so this is not a scale-blind
   pre-registration. The claim this freeze supports is the narrower, honest
   one: the pipeline's cloud-unit geometry (per-facet area and pitch, and the
   candidate and fallback span values in cloud units) is locked before any
   real-world conversion or comparison is computed. The tape value and the
   derived multiplier are deliberately not in this file.

2. The candidate slot is the instrument the scale calc will use, not a record
   of what was predicted. The candidate is the ridge length:r6,7, the span
   that physically exists and was taped. The originally predicted rank-1 span
   lines:j0,3-j0,5 was found NON-EXISTENT on the roof: dormer points corrupted
   facet 0's junctions with facets 3 and 5, so its derived junction lines, and
   the span between them, are not real geometry. It is deliberately NOT in the
   candidate slot. It is preserved as predicted-but-refuted here and in the
   DECISIONS.md entry of 2026-07-15. The prediction being wrong is a validation
   finding kept visible, not the declared instrument.

3. Fallback. The declared fallback is lines:r1,3-e1 (the slope span of facet 1,
   the perpendicular between ridge 1,3 and eave 1), to be used only if the
   primary ridge measurement fails. It is endpoint-free (the high endpoint
   uncertainty of ridge 1,3 does not enter it), it uses a clean unflagged eave
   (eave 1) and a validated true ridge (1,3), and it is reachable from the eave
   side (hook the drip edge, run the tape up the slope), a different access
   than walking the primary ridge. Its predicted error is higher than the
   primary (about 1.1% area vs about 0.8%). Caveat: facet 1 carries dormer
   contamination in its overall area and pitch, but the two features this span
   uses (the eave-1 edge and the ridge-1,3 line) are individually clean.

4. Unresolved dormers contaminate per-facet numbers. About 8 dormers were not
   detected as their own facets; their points were absorbed into other detected
   planes, so specific per-facet areas and pitches are suspect, not only the
   total. Which facets absorbed dormer points could NOT be cleanly determined
   from the cloud. The off-plane signal is 101 entangled high-residual clusters
   that mix genuine dormers, surviving tree/foliage (this cloud's known
   adversary), and an infinite-plane assignment artifact, with residuals
   reaching 2 to 3 cloud units (far taller than a dormer); it is not 8 clean
   dormers and the sources are not cleanly separable. The defensible reading:
   facets 4 and 5 are near-clean and least suspect; facet 2 is the heaviest;
   the rest are suspect to varying degrees. Dormer detection is deferred to a
   dedicated effort (see the DECISIONS.md entry of 2026-07-15).
units: cloud units (cu); one tape number converts, later

scale_candidate_primary.tape_plan: on roof, along the line; BOTH ends are eroded edge zone, bias is one-sided (reads short)

scale_candidate_fallback.tape_plan: on roof: hook the drip edge, run up the slope (divergence 0.32 deg, pos-sens 0.045 cu)
